1 JUDGE AND MACT AT CHINCHOLI IN MVC NO.625/2015 AND ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION FROM RS.4,32,520/- TO RS.15,00,000/-.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation, claimant is before this Court in this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 07.05.2014 at about 4:45 p.m. he was proceeding on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-35-R-6946 along with his friend Raju as pillion rider.

When they were near Degree College of Sulepeth, a Hero Honda motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-32-EC-3116 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle' for short) came from the opposite side and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.

Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital,
Sulepeth and from there to Chirayu Hospital, Gulbarga.
Despite of prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
The injuries have resulted in permanent partial disability.
4. In respect of the accident, criminal case was registered against the rider of the offending vehicle and charge-sheet was filed.
At the time of accident, petitioner was working as a driver.
Now he is unable to work as he used to and suffering loss of income.
As owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. Though respondents duly served with summons and appeared through counsel, respondent No.1 failed to file written statement.
6. Respondent No.2 remained ex parte.
7. In support of his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and one witness as PW.2.

He has relied upon Exs.P1 to 14.
8.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition and granted compensation in a sum of Rs.4,32,520/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the compensation with interest.
9. The details of the compensation as granted as below:

10.
Respondent No.2 has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
11. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that though the disability is calculated at 52% of the whole body, the Tribunal has erred in considering it as 18%.
The income taken at Rs.6,000/- is on the lower side.
The compensation granted under all the remaining heads are also on the lower side and requires enhancement.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supports the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.
13. It is relevant to note that at the request of counsel for appellant/petitioner vide order dated 14.12.2021 the petitioner was referred to Medical Board for reassessment of the disability.

However,
today learned counsel for the appellant/petitioner submitted that though the petitioner has approached the Civil Hospital as well as GIMS, he has not been examined and the reassessment of disability is not done and he is being sent from one Hospital to other and prays to decide the appeal based on material placed on record.
In the light of his submission, the order dated 14.12.2021 is recalled.
14. In fact the appellant/petitioner was present before the Court and this Court interacted with him and observed that he is having slight limp while walking.
He submitted that at present he is driving auto rickshaw.

15. Heard arguments and perused the records.
16.
The fact that as on the date of accident the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.2 is not in dispute.

Based on the complaint filed by the petitioner, after Shivakumar vs Padmakar And Anr on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184834896/
3 conducting detailed investigation the concerned police have filed charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The testimony of PW.1 and 2 coupled with documents placed on record to prove the fact that petitioner sustained the injuries in question in the accident involving the offending vehicle.
In the light of the same, the only issue left to be examined is whether the compensation granted to the petitioner is just and reasonable or it requires enhancement under the following heads.
17. Loss of future earnings:
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.2,20,320/-.
The accident dated 07.05.2014.
Based on medical records the Tribunal has correctly considered the age of petitioner as 24 years and appropriate multiplier '18'.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal has taken the income of the petitioner on notional basis at Rs.6,000/-.
Since the accident is of the year 2014, based on minimum wages, it ought to have been taken at Rs.7,500/- per month.
The Tribunal has not granted loss of future prospects as required under Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma Insurance Company case).

sentences.text: Since the petitioner was aged less than 40 years, 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.
Therefore, income of the petitioner is required to be taken at Rs.10,500/-.
PW.2 has deposed that petitioner has sustained 52% disability of the whole body.
(2018) 18 SCC 130 He is not a treating doctor.
There is no basis for coming to such conclusion.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly taken the whole body disability at 18%.
With these components the compensation under this head works out to be Rs.10,500/- x 12 x 18 x 18% = Rs.4,08,240/-.
18. Medical Expenses:
Based on the medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.1,59,200/- and the same does not call for interference.
19. Pain and suffering & Loss of amenities of life:
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.25,000/- and Rs.10,000/- under these heads.
Having regard to the fact that petitioner has suffered permanent partial disability, this is on the lower side.

The same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-
and 20,000/-.
20.
Attendant charges, food and conveyance:
Under this head the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.6,000/-.
Having regard to the nature of injuries suffered, it is on the lower side.
The same is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
21. Compensation for laid up period:
Having regard to the nature of injuries suffered and treatment taken, it would be reasonable to expect him to be under treatment for a period of three months.

Hence, at the rate of Rs.7,500/- he is entitled for compensation of Rs.22,500/- as against Rs.12,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
22.

Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation in a sum of Rs.6,59,940/- with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.4,32,520/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

1 . Loss of future Rs.2,20,320/- Rs.4,08,240/-
 earnings

2. Medical Expenses Rs.1,59,200/- Rs.1,59,200/-
 3. Pain and suffering Rs.25,000/- Rs.40,000/-

4 . Attendant charges, Rs.6,000/- Rs.10,000/-
 food and  conveyance  5. Compensation for Rs.12,000/- 22,500/-
 laid up period  6. loss of amenities Rs.10,000/- Rs.20,000/-
To this extent, the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a.
Appeal is allowed in part.
b. Appellant/petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.6,59,940/- as against Rs.4,32,520/- granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation.

c. Respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation together with accrued interest within a period of six weeks from the date of this order (minus the compensation already paid/deposited) on the enhanced compensation.
d. Registry is directed to return the TCR along with copy of this order to the Tribunal.
